answer: A network can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to stake a refundable deposit tied to a single verifiable hardware attestation — a ferrous anchor, like a TPM-backed key, that cannot be cloned cheaply. New identities join a delta queue: they earn trust slowly, with voting weight rising only as they complete verified tasks over time, so a flood of fresh sybils stays at the vertex of low influence. An attacker must buy real hardware and wait out the ramp for every identity, making mass fakery cost-linear instead of free.
